full_judgment: 11. The trial Court failed to consider the implication of section 26G of Bengal Tenancy Act, which was inserted in the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1928 curtailing the period of usufructuary mortgage to a maximum period of 15 years. Even if the mortgage might have been created for 50 years, that period having been reduced by a statute to a maximum period of 15 years, it cannot be said that the mortgages created by the predecessors of the plaintiff continued even after lapse of the period of 15 years. So the suit for declaration of title with consequential relief which was filed on 30.03.1983 was maintainable. Whatever the right of the plaintiffs and their predecessors had in the suit land that right stood extinguished with the sale of the suit land in auction 1983. The trial Court failed to consider the factual and legal aspects of the case in passing the judgment and decree of the suit.
